The best colleges for paleontology include the University of Michigan, Bowling Green State University, UC Berkeley, the University of Kansas and Yale University. Michigan is our best all-round US choice because it combines a formal Paleontology minor with museum research, fossil preparation and access to a collection of more than four million specimens. Bowling Green offers one of the clearest specialist bachelor’s routes, while Berkeley and Kansas stand out for graduate research.

Outside the USA, the University of Alberta, Bristol and Birmingham provide more direct undergraduate pathways.

Here’s the thing: many of the best paleontology schools do not offer a degree called “Paleontology”. Students often begin with geology, Earth sciences, biology or evolutionary biology, then specialise through fossils, fieldwork, museum collections and postgraduate research.

That distinction matters. A famous research university may be an excellent PhD destination but a poor fit for someone seeking a direct bachelor’s degree.

This is not a ranking based only on publication volume or university fame. We ranked student fit: programme clarity, access to fossils, museum or laboratory resources, field training, undergraduate accessibility and progression into research.

What We Found After Reviewing These Programmes

Only a minority of the universities in this guide offer a named undergraduate palaeontology degree.

Three provide particularly direct bachelor’s routes: Alberta, Bristol and Birmingham. BGSU offers a formal paleobiology specialisation, while Michigan and Washington offer defined minors alongside broader science degrees.

The remaining universities are strongest as research environments. At Berkeley, Kansas, Yale, Chicago and Harvard, students usually study geology, biology or Earth sciences before moving into specialist research.

That is mildly counterintuitive. The most famous palaeontology research centre is not automatically the best place to begin your undergraduate education.

How We Selected the Best Paleontology Colleges

  • active palaeontology or paleobiology research;
  • a clear degree, specialisation, minor or graduate route;
  • fossil collections or museum access;
  • fieldwork or fossil-preparation opportunities;
  • undergraduate research or a strong postgraduate pathway;
  • current programme information.

We also considered limitations. A huge museum collection carries less value for an undergraduate if students cannot use it. Likewise, a course with “Paleontology” in its title may be weaker than a geology degree with active researchers, field training and a serious fossil laboratory.

1. University of Michigan - Best Overall

The University of Michigan offers one of the most balanced paleontology college experiences in the USA.

Students can combine a broader major with a formal Paleontology minor. The minor introduces the fossil record, historical-science methods and theoretical questions through entry, core and advanced courses.

The university’s Museum of Paleontology gives students more than classroom exposure. Undergraduates may join research projects, prepare fossils, complete senior theses and participate through the Undergraduate Research Opportunities Program. The museum’s research centre holds more than four million fossil specimens.

A concrete example: past undergraduate work has included moulding and casting a mastodon skeleton and learning professional fossil-preparation techniques.

Best for: students seeking a flexible US science degree with a recognised palaeontology pathway.

Watch out for: Paleontology is a minor, not a standalone bachelor’s major. Students need to choose a suitable primary subject, normally Earth and Environmental Sciences or another relevant science.

Latest cost guide: Michigan’s official 2026–27 budget places the annual cost for a lower-division non-resident undergraduate at approximately US$88,400, including tuition, living expenses, books, transport and personal costs.

2. Bowling Green State University - Best Specialist US Bachelor’s Route

Bowling Green State University is not as famous as Harvard or Berkeley. For some undergraduate students, it may be the more useful choice.

Its Geology BS with a Paleobiology specialisation combines geological training with biology, evolution and fossil-based research. Students complete at least 122 credits, including substantial geology and specialist coursework.

The curriculum includes subjects such as Life through Time, Vertebrate Paleontology, Evolution, genetics, geospatial science and independent research. Students also complete intensive field training across regions such as the Basin and Range Province, Colorado Plateau and Rocky Mountains.

Laboratory access extends beyond palaeontology. Students can use geochemistry, remote-sensing, sediment-core and rock-preparation facilities.

Best for: students who want palaeobiology to remain visible throughout their bachelor’s degree.

Watch out for: BGSU has a specialist and practical structure, but it does not provide the same scale of research collections as Michigan, Yale or Berkeley.

3. University of California, Berkeley - Best for Graduate Paleobiology

UC Berkeley works best for students who see palaeontology as a research career rather than simply an undergraduate subject.

The University of California Museum of Paleontology connects research across fossils, evolution, living organisms and the history of life. Students typically enter through Integrative Biology, Earth and Planetary Science or a related discipline.

Berkeley’s value lies in its research ecosystem. Students can work around major fossil collections, laboratories and researchers studying macroevolution, extinction, morphology, ecology and Earth-life interactions.

Best for: graduate paleobiology, macroevolution and collection-based research.

Watch out for: Berkeley does not provide a straightforward standalone undergraduate paleontology major. An undergraduate must build the route through a broader science degree.

Latest cost guide: a current official Berkeley estimate places a non-resident undergraduate budget at roughly US$93,700 per year before financial aid, depending on housing and personal expenses.

Berkeley can be an outstanding PhD destination. It may not be the most economical place to complete the science foundation that comes before one.

4. University of Kansas - Best for Funded Graduate Research

The University of Kansas is one of the best paleontology schools for students interested in graduate research.

Its Biodiversity Institute supports vertebrate palaeontology, invertebrate palaeontology and paleobotany. Graduate study normally runs through Ecology and Evolutionary Biology or Geology, with access to museum collections and specialist curators.

That can change the real cost dramatically.

Best for: funded MA or PhD research, museum collections and fossil invertebrates or vertebrates.

Watch out for: Kansas is stronger as a graduate destination than as a direct undergraduate paleontology degree.

Students considering this path should first compare suitable master’s-level options across America, then contact researchers whose work genuinely matches their interests.

5. Yale University - Best for Vertebrate Fossils

Yale combines Earth science with one of North America’s most important fossil collections.

The Yale Peabody Museum’s vertebrate palaeontology division holds more than 80,000 catalogued specimens, including nearly 5,000 type specimens. Its holdings span every vertebrate class and range from the Ordovician to the Holocene.

Students and researchers can work with preparation laboratories, mechanical preparation, moulding, casting, histology, micro-CT scanning, photogrammetry and surface scanning.

Yale’s invertebrate collection adds an estimated 4.5 million specimens, giving the university unusual depth across multiple branches of palaeontology.

Best for: vertebrate palaeontology, systematics, evolution and museum-based research.

Watch out for: Yale does not offer a simple undergraduate degree called Paleontology. Students generally build a route through Earth and Planetary Sciences, Ecology and Evolutionary Biology or Anthropology.

Latest cost guide: Yale’s published undergraduate budget totals about US$97,985 before travel and any health-insurance adjustment.

The sticker price does not tell the whole story. Yale evaluates international applicants without considering their ability to pay and meets demonstrated financial need through need-based aid.

6. University of Chicago - Best for Evolution and Deep Time

The University of Chicago suits students who want to study the history of life through evolution, extinction, climate and planetary change.

Its Department of the Geophysical Sciences studies the history of life alongside oceans, atmospheres, the solid Earth and planetary formation. Facilities include rock and fossil preparation, scanning electron microscopy, mass spectrometry and geochemical laboratories.

Chicago’s strength is intellectual range. A student might approach an extinction event through fossils, sedimentary evidence, evolutionary theory, climate modelling and geochemistry rather than treating palaeontology as an isolated subject.

Best for: evolutionary research, mass extinction, geobiology and quantitative Earth science.

Watch out for: this is an indirect and academically demanding route. Students need comfort with mathematics, chemistry, physics or computational analysis alongside fossils.

7. Harvard University - Best for Research Breadth

Harvard’s palaeobiology work spans the deep Precambrian to recent geological history.

The university’s paleobiology faculty use fieldwork, functional morphology, phylogenetics, isotopic analysis and theoretical methods. The Museum of Comparative Zoology holds approximately 21 million living and fossil vertebrate and invertebrate specimens across its collections.

Students normally enter through Organismic and Evolutionary Biology or Earth and Planetary Sciences.

Best for: broad evolutionary research and access to major zoological collections.

Watch out for: Harvard’s research reputation does not translate into a direct bachelor’s major in paleontology. Applicants must build the correct course and research combination.

Latest cost guide: Harvard’s 2026–27 published costs amount to approximately US$95,100–100,100 when billed charges, books, personal expenses and possible travel are included.

International students can receive institutional financial aid on the same basis as US students. Harvard states that it meets 100% of demonstrated financial need.

8. University of Washington - Best Flexible Undergraduate Pathway

The University of Washington offers a 30-credit Paleobiology minor that students can add to a relevant major.

The programme brings together biology, Earth and space sciences and biological anthropology. Its research areas include early life, mass extinction, mammal origins, ancient climate transitions and the spread of grasslands.

Students can take subjects such as Analytical Paleobiology, Vertebrate Paleontology, Invertebrate Paleontology and Paleobiology Field Methods and Research. The Burke Museum’s fossil collections provide an important local research resource.

Best for: combining palaeontology with biology, geology, Earth science or anthropology.

Latest cost guide: Washington’s estimated annual non-resident undergraduate cost is about US$67,800 for a student living on or off campus.

Students comparing this route with other institutions may find it useful to explore US universities that regularly serve international applicants.

9. South Dakota Mines - Best Practical Master’s Programme

South Dakota Mines offers a dedicated MS in Paleontology with thesis and non-thesis options.

Featured subjects include Paleobiology, Field Paleontology, Vertebrate Fossil Preparation and Conservation, Museum Exhibit Design, quantitative methods and palaeontological resource management.

The course connects scientific research with practical museum and field skills. That is useful for students considering work in fossil preparation, collections, public agencies, museums or mitigation palaeontology.

Best for: practical graduate training and field-oriented career preparation.

Watch out for: applicants normally need a relevant bachelor’s background. The thesis route is eligible for assistantships, while the non-thesis route is not.

Latest cost guide: South Dakota Mines estimates total annual international graduate expenses at US$32,150. Around half of its graduate students receive assistantships, mainly in thesis-based master’s and doctoral programmes. Qualifying assistantships can provide a full tuition and programme-fee reduction.

The university also lists an US$6,000 Ivanhoe Fellowship for eligible MS students from countries including Bangladesh, Nepal, Nigeria and Turkey, although it requires a departmental nomination and matching assistantship.

10. University of Alberta - Best Direct Canadian Major

The University of Alberta offers one of the most direct paleontology degree routes in North America.

Students can pursue a BSc major or honours pathway drawing from Earth and Atmospheric Sciences and Biological Sciences. Current course listings include palaeontology, vertebrate paleobiology, specialist topics and a field school.

The Paleontology Field School teaches fossil collection, curation and analysis at major dinosaur sites in Western Canada. Geology field training also covers sedimentary rocks, stratigraphy, fossil identification and reconstruction of ancient environments.

Best for: a named undergraduate programme with Canadian field experience.

Watch out for: field schools may carry additional instructional costs. International students should use Alberta’s official fee calculator rather than relying on a generic estimate.

11. University of Bristol - Best UK Palaeontology and Evolution Degree

Bristol offers a direct BSc Palaeontology and Evolution for 2027 entry, alongside an MSci option.

The course mixes biology and Earth science from the first year. Later study includes evolutionary palaeobiology, vertebrate biomechanics, microfossils, ancient climates and research methods.

Dedicated palaeontology field trips are included in the tuition fee. Students may also pursue laboratory internships, outreach work and a final-year research project.

Best for: students who want a clear degree title combining fossils, biology and geology.

Watch out for: the degree has a quantitative side. Students should expect statistics, analytical methods and scientific research, not only fossil identification.

Latest fee guide: Bristol’s 2027 course page displays an international first-year fee of £31,300, but states that this is the latest published 2026-entry amount. The final 2027 fee will be confirmed later and may rise.

Students considering UK universities should review the course details, admission requirements, academic pathways, and available UK higher education guidance.

12. University of Birmingham - Best for Palaeontology and Geology

Birmingham’s Palaeontology and Geology BSc places fossils firmly within geological science.

Students complete fieldwork, laboratory training and research-led study. The course connects with the Lapworth Museum of Geology, which holds more than 250,000 specimens, and facilities used for geochemistry and fossil investigation.

Compulsory fieldwork has recently included locations in Britain and overseas, with the university covering travel and accommodation for required field courses under its current arrangement.

Best for: geology, field mapping, museum skills and fossil interpretation.

Watch out for: international tuition for 2027 entry was not confirmed when this guide was checked. Applicants should use the university’s country and fee selector before budgeting.

Which Colleges Offer a Paleontology Major?

Colleges with paleontology programs use several different structures.

The University of Alberta offers a direct major or honours route. Bristol and Birmingham offer named UK palaeontology degrees. BGSU provides a Geology BS with a Paleobiology specialisation.

Michigan and Washington offer formal minors. Berkeley, Kansas, Yale, Chicago and Harvard teach palaeontology through broader science departments and research groups.

So the short answer is yes, but paleontology major colleges are less common than geology or biology programmes with fossil-based specialisation.

Best Undergraduate Paleontology Programs

The strongest direct undergraduate choices are:

  • University of Alberta for a named North American major;
  • University of Bristol for palaeontology, evolution and biology;
  • University of Birmingham for fossils grounded in geology;
  • Bowling Green State University for a specialist US bachelor’s route;
  • University of Michigan for a minor, museum research and fossil preparation;
  • University of Washington for an interdisciplinary paleobiology minor.

A direct title can make course selection easier. It is not automatically better.

A geology degree with field mapping, stratigraphy and undergraduate research may prepare a student more effectively than a narrow course with limited practical work.

Best Graduate Schools for Paleontology

UC Berkeley, Kansas, Yale, Chicago, Harvard, Michigan and South Dakota Mines are strong graduate options, but students should not shortlist them by name alone.

Start with the Paleontological Society’s graduate programme directory, then check:

  • whether a relevant supervisor is accepting students;
  • whether the necessary specimens or equipment are available;
  • whether the programme supports fieldwork and conference travel;
  • where recent graduates work.

Contact the potential supervisor only after reading their recent work. Generic emails are easy to spot.

What Should You Major in to Become a Paleontologist?

Geology or Earth sciences is often the strongest foundation for field-based palaeontology. These subjects teach sedimentology, stratigraphy, geological time, mapping and the interpretation of ancient environments.

Biology works well for evolution, anatomy, ecology and paleobiology. Anthropology may suit students interested in human evolution or certain vertebrate questions.

Think about it this way. A student studying marine reptiles needs to understand the rocks around the fossil. A researcher modelling how an extinct animal moved needs anatomy, biomechanics and data analysis.

Useful supporting subjects include:

  • statistics;
  • GIS;
  • chemistry;
  • evolutionary biology;
  • comparative anatomy;
  • scientific programming;
  • research writing.

Many professional research and university careers eventually require a master’s or PhD.

How to Choose the Best Paleontology College

Do not choose by brand name alone.

First, check the current faculty. A university may advertise a historic palaeontology reputation even though the researcher who built it left years ago.

Then inspect the modules. Look for sedimentology, stratigraphy, evolution, fossil preparation, field methods, quantitative analysis and research projects.

Museum access also needs scrutiny. Ask whether undergraduates can work with collections, join laboratories or complete a thesis. A museum beside the campus is not enough.

Finally, compare the complete cost. Undergraduate debt matters because many palaeontologists continue into postgraduate study.

Students still comparing institutional types can review lower-cost public options in America before committing to an expensive private university.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are the best colleges for paleontology?

The best colleges for paleontology include Michigan, BGSU, Berkeley, Kansas, Yale, Chicago, Harvard, Washington, South Dakota Mines, Alberta, Bristol and Birmingham. The right choice depends on whether you need an undergraduate degree, a minor, fieldwork or graduate research.

What are the best colleges for paleontology in the USA?

Michigan is a strong all-round choice, BGSU offers a specialist bachelor’s route, and Washington provides a formal paleobiology minor. Berkeley, Kansas, Yale, Chicago and Harvard are particularly strong for research and graduate study.

What are the best paleontology schools in the world?

Strong international options include the University of Alberta in Canada and Bristol and Birmingham in the UK. The USA has a wider range of museum-linked and research-intensive universities, but fewer direct undergraduate degrees than many applicants expect.

What is the best college for undergraduate paleontology?

Alberta is one of the clearest direct North American choices. Bristol and Birmingham offer named UK degrees, while BGSU provides a specialist US pathway. Michigan is particularly useful for students who want a broader degree plus a formal minor and museum experience.

Can I major in paleontology?

Yes, although direct majors are uncommon. Alberta offers a direct programme, Bristol and Birmingham have named UK degrees, and BGSU offers a paleobiology specialisation. Many other students major in geology, Earth sciences or biology.

Do I need a PhD to become a paleontologist?

A PhD is normally expected for independent academic research, university teaching and many senior museum roles. Some fossil-preparation, field, collections, education and technical jobs may accept a bachelor’s or master’s degree with strong practical experience.

Is geology or biology better for paleontology?

Geology is usually better for rocks, fieldwork, stratigraphy and depositional environments. Biology is stronger for evolution, anatomy and living systems. Many successful palaeontologists combine both.

Is paleontology a good career?

It can be rewarding, but it is specialised and competitive. Graduates may work in museums, universities, geological surveys, government agencies, environmental consulting, fossil-resource management, teaching or science communication.

Final Advice

The best colleges for paleontology give students three things: strong science training, meaningful access to fossils or fieldwork, and a realistic route into research.

Decide first whether you need a direct undergraduate degree or a broader science pathway. Then compare current faculty, modules, collections, field training and net cost.

Do not choose a university because it has the biggest dinosaur in its entrance hall.

Choose the place where you can build evidence of your own ability: field notes, laboratory skills, a research project, quantitative experience and strong academic references.

For personal help comparing countries, costs and suitable routes, you can discuss your study plan with an adviser.
